items.title: Health checks aur failover: mara hua server request kyun leta rehta hai
items.one_idea: A load balancer sends each server a small test request every few seconds (health check); after a set number of consecutive failures it stops routing to that server and the others take over (failover), and the interval times the threshold sets how long a dead server still receives requests.
items.spoken_hook: Server मर गया, फिर भी request वहीं जाती रही।
items.hook_formula: surprising_fact: with default settings a dead server keeps receiving requests for about interval x threshold seconds (30 s x 2 checks = about 60 s, arithmetic from the AWS defaults), the viewer's own request is the one that fails
items.hook_10s: Server मर गया, फिर भी request वहीं जाती रही। Load balancer हर server से बार-बार पूछता है: ठीक हो? जवाब न आए, तो उसे बाहर कर देता है। इसे health check कहते हैं। [frame 0: four server boxes behind a balancer, one box greyed with a cross, request dots still flowing into it]

items.visual_idea: One fixed frame: a balancer on the left and four server boxes on the right. Small request dots flow in a round and one box greys out with a cross while dots still pile into it; then a ping travels to each box and comes back, the silent box collects red ticks (1, 2) and a gate closes in front of it so the dots go only to the other three; at the end its ping returns, green ticks fill (1 to 5) and the gate opens. A two-ended bar shows detection time = interval x threshold, short bar vs long bar.
items.everyday_anchor: A dhaba manager calls out 'ready?' to each cook before sending orders; a cook who does not answer twice gets no more order slips until he answers again.
items.example: EXAMPLE: 4 servers behind one balancer, round robin, one dead and not yet detected: 1 of every 4 requests (25 percent) fails. EXAMPLE: check every 30 s with 2 failures needed means up to about 60 s of requests to the dead server; every 5 s with 2 failures means about 10 s but 6 times more check requests. All server counts and traffic are invented.
facts_to_verify: AWS ALB (fetched 2026-11-07): the balancer sends a health check request to each target every HealthCheckIntervalSeconds (default 30 for instance/ip targets, range 5-300); UnhealthyThresholdCount default 2 (range 2-10) consecutive failures takes the target out of service; HealthyThresholdCount default 5 consecutive successes puts it back; timeout default 5 s; path default /; success code default 200; it routes only to healthy targets.
AWS ALB: if a target group has only unhealthy targets the balancer fails open and sends requests to all of them regardless of health. This is the catch beat.

NGINX: passive checks (max_fails default 1, fail_timeout default 10 s) mark a server unavailable after failures seen on live traffic; active checks are NGINX Plus only (interval default 5 s). Say 'for example NGINX and AWS defaults differ', do not call one right.
Wikipedia Failover: failover = switching to a redundant or standby system when the active one fails, automatic; heartbeat between two servers is one detection method. Switchover needs a human.

The 60 s and 10 s figures are our arithmetic from interval x threshold on AWS defaults; say 'about' and 'with default settings'. Actual detection also depends on timeout and where in the interval the failure happens.

Not sourced, keep out of the script: any claim that a short interval causes false positives at a named company, any cost figure, 'health check must hit the database'. False positive (a slow but alive server marked out) is stated as a typical risk of a tight threshold, not as a measured number.
No code on screen; if any is added, run it and show its real output.
